annotations.title: Man hu! what is this!.
annotations.text: [1] VVhen the people of Iſrael in the deſert had ſpent their prouiſion of meate brought from Ægypt, and according to Gods promiſe had receiued ſtore of quails; going forth in the morning they ſawe a ſtrange thing lye vpon the ground like to hoare froſt, whereat marveling they ſaid one to another What is this! in their language Man hu! Whereupon ſaith Theodoret (q. 30. in Exod.) their demand vvas turned into the name, and it was called Manna. VVhich as the ſame and other ancient Doctors gather by the holie Scriptures, was a wonderful and miraculous meate, [2] and withal a figure of a more excellent thing, long after promiſed, and geuen by our B. Sauiour, in the holie Sacrament of the Euchariſt. As witneſſe S. Gregorie Nyſſen (Enar. vitæ Moyſi, circa medium) S. Ambroſe (li. de ijs qui Myſt. initian. cap. 8.) S. Cyril Alexandrinus, S. Chryſoſtom, S. Auguſtine, Theophilact and others [3], vpon the ſixth of S. Iohn. VVhere alſo the text of our Sauiours long diſcourſe with the Capharnaites, sheweth euidently that he promiſed to give a farre better meate then Manna, to thoſe that believed in him. I am, (ſaith our Lord) the bread of life, which deſcended from heauen; your fathers did eate Manna in the deſert, and died. The bread which I vvil give is my flesh, for the life of the vvorld. My flesh is meate indeed, and my blood is drink indeede &c. S. Paul likewiſe teacheth (1. Cor. 10.) that this Manna, and the water iſſuing out of the rocke, were figures of the ſame B. Sacrament, as is noted in thoſe places. Here only we commend to the Chriſtian readers remembrance that the thing figured doth euer excede the figure according to S. Pauls doctrin (Colloſ. 2.) wiſhing him therefore to conſider, [4] that in Manna [5] were at leaſt twelue clear miracles. [6] Firſt, it was made by Angels whereof it is called, the bread of Angels. [7] Secondly, it was not produced from the earth, nor water, as ordinarie meats are, but came from the ayre. [8] Thirdly, how faſt or ſlowly ſoeuer anie man did gather it, in the end each one had the ſame meaſure ful, called a gomor, and no more nor leſſe. [9] Fourthly, the ſixth day which was next before the Sabbath, that which they gathered, was found to be double portions to other days, that is, two gomors for euerie one. [10] Fifthly, there fell none at all on the Sabbath day. [11] Sixthly, if in the reſt of the weke anie part was left all night, it putrefied and was corrupt in the morning, but the night before the Sabbath day, it remained ſound and good. [12] Seventhly, notwithſtanding diuerſitie of ſtomachs in ſo great a multitude, the ſame meaſure was ſufficient and no more, to euerie one, young and old and of middle age. [13] Eighthly, the heat of the ſunne melted and conſumed that which remained in the field, though otherwiſe it endured heat of the fire, ſeething in water, grinding in mills, and beating in mortars. [14] Ninthly, it taſted to euerie one, what they deſired. [15] Tenthly, it ſeemed neuertheleſſe to the euil minded, loathſome and light meate, but pleaſant to the good. [16] Eleventhly, part of it was kept in the Arke by Gods commandment, and was not corrupted in manie hundred years. [17] Twelfthly, this ſtrange and extraordinarie prouiſion continued forty years, that is, til the children of Iſrael came to the promiſed land, and then ceaſed. ◦ You ſee then ſo miraculous a figure farre excelled Zuinglius' or Caluins communion bread, which containeth no miracle at all, only ſignifying Chriſts body. But, as our Sauiours owne words importe, and ancient fathers teach vs, by Manna was prefigured Chriſts verie body and blood, with his ſoule and Diuinitie vnder the form of bread. [18] For this indeede infinitely excelleth Manna, containing all the foreſaid, or rather much more eminent miracles. [19] For firſt, it was conſecrated by the maruelous power of Chriſts word, and euer ſince the ſame is done, by the like power communicated to Prieſts, [20] (2) in his Church militant, [21] (3) one and the verie ſame, and not manie, in innumerable places, and in euerie leſſe or greater form, yea in the leaſt particle of the accidents that may be, Chriſt is whole and entire. [22] (4) It giveth abundance of grace in this life, ſignified by the day before the Sabbath, for the glory of the next life in eternal reſt, [23] (5) where is no more vſe of Sacraments, but euerlaſting fruition of glory. [24] (6) Whoſoever therefore would make temporal commoditie of this heauenlie foode, as it were reſeruing Manna for other days of the weke, it periſheth to him, and turneth to his ignominie, but being reſerued in the faithful ſoule, for the life to come, which is the true Sabbath, it remaineth in heauenlie treaſure. [25] (7) And ſo it auaileth to euerie one, as their ſoule, which is the ſpiritual ſtomach of ſupernatural meate, is leſſe or more diſpoſed. [26] (8) Though heat of perſecution, and other aduerſe power take away this Sacrament and Sacrifice abroad in the field of this world, yet no power extinguiſheth it within the Church, where it is in due maner prepared & miniſtered to the children of God, [27] (9.) where it yeldeth all comfort, ſtrength & contentment to good ſpiritual deſires, [28] (10.) but to the incredulous Capharnaites ſemeth vnpoſſible, and to carnal conceits loathſome. [29] (11.) Being worthily receiued into our mortal bodies, our arke or temporal tabernacle, it remaineth in incorruptible effect, whereby the body shall be raiſed againe from death, and together with the ſoule be eternally glorified. [30] (12.) In the meane time of this pilgrimage of mankind, it is our way-faring ſpecial prouiſion, dailie and ſuperſubſtantial bread, til we ſhal poſſeſſe the promiſed land, the Kingdome of heauen in eternal bliſſe.

notes.text: It was a figure of the Eucharist,
Psal 77. v 25 Roffen. li. 1. c 12 cont. Oecolamp. D. Hesk li. 3 c 12 parlam.
Al the said miracles are more eminent in the B. Sacrament.
